incidents.ackNotDispatchedTitle: Tracker still in its cancel window
incidents.ackNotDispatchedBody: The alarm has not dispatched yet, so it cannot be acknowledged. Wait for the dispatch, then acknowledge it. The tracker rejects an acknowledgement during the countdown.
incidents.resolveUnconfirmedBody: The tracker did not confirm the acknowledgement. This includes a tracker that rebooted or lost power, which boots idle and no longer knows the incident. The alarm may still sound until the device is powered off or acknowledges. Use this only when the tracker cannot be reached.
incidents.resolveUnconfirmedConfirmHelp: The tracker did not confirm the alarm stopped. It may still sound until the device is powered off or acknowledges.
incidents.confirmFalseAlarm: Ask the tracker to stop the alert and mark this incident as a false alarm? The incident closes only when the tracker confirms.
incidents.confirmFalseAlarmLocal: Mark this incident as a false alarm? This closes the incident.
incidents.confirmCancel: Ask the tracker to stop the alert? The incident stays open until the tracker confirms, and a confirmed stop closes it as a false alarm.
incidents.cancelRequested: Cancel requested. Waiting for the tracker.
incidents.ackRequested: Acknowledgement requested. Waiting for the tracker.
incidents.cancelWaitingBody: Waiting for the tracker to confirm. The alert may keep running until it does.
incidents.cancelWaitingBlocksAck: Acknowledge is unavailable until the tracker answers this cancel request.
incidents.cancelNotConfirmedBody: The tracker did not confirm that the alert stopped. Check the tracker before treating this as closed.
incidents.cancelTooLateBody: The tracker replied that the alert was already sent, so it could not stop it.
incidents.cancelUnknownIncidentBody: The tracker does not know this incident, so the alert was not stopped.
incidents.cancelExpiredBody: The tracker never collected the cancel request. The alert may still be running.
incidents.cancelFailedBody: The tracker reported that the cancel failed. Check the tracker.

incidents.errorAckRequired: Acknowledge this incident before resolving it. The tracker alarm is still latched.
incidents.errorAckNotDispatched: The tracker is still in its cancel window. Wait until the alert dispatches, then acknowledge it.

provisioning.title: WiFi setup
provisioning.description: An installer joins the tracker's setup network and enters the WiFi details and a device token. WiFi is used only during setup; alerts still travel over 4G.
provisioning.stateNote: Setup state comes from the last heartbeat, not a live WiFi check.
provisioning.deviceIdHint: The tracker's MAC address, exactly as shown.
provisioning.setupAddressHint: Open this address after joining the setup network.
provisioning.tokenBody: The server stores only a hash of the token, so the current one cannot be shown. Rotate it to show a new token once. The old token stops working immediately, so enter the new one on the tracker.
provisioning.step1Body: Do not hold either reset button. A tracker without a saved network opens the setup network by itself. If it already has one, use the WiFi reset below.
provisioning.step2Body: On the phone, open WiFi settings and join {apName}. It is open, so no password is needed.
provisioning.step3Body: Open http://192.168.4.1 in the phone browser. If a sign-in prompt appears, use it.
provisioning.step4Body: Pick the WiFi network or type its name. The tracker sees 2.4 GHz networks only. Enter the WiFi password, confirm the Device ID matches the one above, and enter the new Device Token.
provisioning.step5Body: Tap Connect and save. The tracker tests the network and saves only after it joins. The setup network closes on its own.
provisioning.resetIntro: Both buttons work only in the first 60 seconds after power-on. Power on with the button released, wait 5 seconds, then press and hold.
provisioning.wifiResetBody: Hold 5 seconds, then release. Clears the saved WiFi and restarts. The Device ID and token are kept.
provisioning.factoryResetBody: Hold 10 seconds. Clears WiFi, Device ID, token and the provisioned marker, then restarts. Rotate the token here before you set the tracker up again.
provisioning.resetCancelNote: The cancel button stays with the alert and never resets the tracker.
provisioning.credentialsNoteTitle: No WiFi credentials are stored here
provisioning.credentialsNote: This page cannot save WiFi credentials. The WiFi password is entered only on the tracker's setup page and is never stored on the server.
provisioning.portalNote: The setup network is open and closes by itself after 10 minutes.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.body: LifeLink stores vehicle location and crash telemetry to deliver emergency alerts. Location data is available only to members of your organization. The retention periods in Settings are enforced by a scheduled daily cleanup: telemetry and incident records older than the configured period are deleted automatically. Incident evidence is kept for the configured period because it may be needed for insurance or legal review.
privacy.extra: Telemetry and incident evidence have separate retention settings, and each organization's settings apply to its own data. The cleanup removes old rows in bounded batches and records counts in an audit log. Members of other organizations cannot query your vehicles or incidents.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.body: LifeLink is a prototype emergency-response aid. It does not replace emergency services, a functioning vehicle, or a qualified driver. Always call local emergency services first.
terms.extra: The platform is provided as-is for a capstone prototype. A missed alert can have consequences beyond the software's control: cellular coverage, GPS visibility, device power, and sensor mounting all matter. Test the installation on the bench and in the vehicle before relying on it.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.subtitle: Delivery targets, the alert log and emergency contacts.
notifications.senderBody: No SMS, email or HTTP sender runs in this build, so alert rows stay Queued. Call emergency services directly.
notifications.policySubtitle: What the intake route does today, read from the incident route and alert templates.
notifications.policyTriggerBody: A device incident report queues alert rows. A suspected incident that is later confirmed queues them if none exist. Incidents the driver cancelled queue none.
notifications.policyTargetsBody: One SMS row per configured phone and one email row per configured email. Targets come from Settings. The HTTP channel exists in the data model but nothing creates HTTP rows.
notifications.policyMessageBody: The SMS template carries the plate, coordinates or location unavailable, GPS age, speed and Philippine time, capped at 320 characters. No sender invokes it yet and no email template exists.
notifications.policyDeliveryBody: Rows are created as Queued. No sender or retry worker is implemented in this codebase, so runtime rows stay Queued until another process updates them.
notifications.policySeverityBody: Severity does not choose targets, channels or escalation. It is a display aid.
notifications.policyEscalationBody: No escalation chain, retry policy or responder dispatch is implemented.
notifications.targetsSubtitle: Phones and emails used when an incident report arrives.
notifications.targetsEmptyBody: Phones and emails configured in Settings appear here.
notifications.targetsNormalizeNote: Numbers must contain 10 to 15 digits after other characters are removed; emails must contain @. Entries that fail are skipped before rows are queued.
notifications.targetsManagedByAdmin: An admin manages alert targets in Settings.

notifications.logEmptyBody: Rows appear when a device reports an incident and alert targets are configured.
